title: Trial Snapshot Playbook — Juno personal tracker
content:
Purpose:
Quick, portable experiment tracking sheet for small inference micro-trials — single-file personal ledger. Use for on-the-fly decisions: change batch/quantize/variant, capture latency & cost delta, and note odd failures. Not a canonical log; meant for fast capture and later export to formal experiment DB.

How I use it (notes to self):
- Run 3 warmup reps, then 10 measured reps. Record median + 95th.
- Cost is a rough per-token estimate based on current cost table (see bottom).
- If p95 > 2x p50 mark as "high tail" and consider smaller batches / lower seq length.
- Add prompt seed and any cache hits/misses.

Quick legend:
- model = model name/variant (e.g., rw-1.1-8b-q3f)
- quant = quantization profile (q8, q4, q3f, fp16)
- seq = input sequence length (tokens)
- batch = tokenizer-level batch size
- kv = prefix/KV cache state (cold/warm/hit%)
- tokens = total tokens generated (estimate)
- p50/p95 = latency ms
- cost_usd = approximate run cost (USD)
- notes = anything weird (OOM, truncation, library warnings)

Table (one-line CSV for quick grep):
#ts,variant,model,quant,seq,batch,kv,tokens,p50_ms,p95_ms,cost_usd,notes
2025-11-03T09:12:21Z,expA,redwood/rw-1.1,fp16,512,4,cold,680,78,210,0.012,baseline cold run
2025-11-03T09:18:05Z,expA,redwood/rw-1.1,q4,512,4,warm(92%),680,60,130,0.008,good perf; tail improved
2025-11-03T09:43:54Z,expB,redwood/rw-1.1-8b,q3f,1024,2,cold,1200,140,460,0.021,heavy tail, spike on first token
2025-11-03T10:02:10Z,expB,redwood/rw-1.1-8b,q3f,1024,2,warm(100%),1200,95,180,0.013,stable after warmup
2025-11-04T14:05:00Z,expC,community-icl-7b,q8,256,8,warm(100%),300,32,60,0.003,cheap but quality drop (repeats)

Micro-aggregates (notes):
- expA: q4 reduces p95 by ~38% vs fp16 when KV warm; p50 improvement ~23%. Cost down ~33% per token.
- expB: q3f gives smallest cost for long seq but shows initial first-token spike; consider pre-warming KV cache or using short warmup TTL.
- expC: q8 is viable for low-cost short prompts but fails on repetition-sensitive tasks.

Immediate actionables (todo):
- [ ] Add a quick script to tag runs with commit sha + region (INF-2142).
- [ ] Capture full token breakdown (input vs output) for next run.
- [ ] Try warmup-only run (send empty prompt) to measure first-token overhead.
- [ ] PR to runtime: log first-token kernel selection time (see linked PR for context).

Heuristics / Rules of Thumb I want to remember:
- If p95/p50 > 2.5 -> reduce batch by 50% or drop seq by 25%
- If cost_usd per 1k tokens > $0.5 on a dedicated test -> try q3f or route to cheaper pool for non-prod
- Warm KV hit% above 85% typically means p95 within 1.6x p50

Quick cost mapping (local rough):
- fp16 baseline: $0.018 per 1k tokens
- q4: ~0.012 per 1k tokens
- q3f: ~0.009 per 1k tokens
- q8 (aggressive): ~0.0035 per 1k tokens
(note: these are personal estimates for fast triage; reconcile with billing before quoting)

Riff notes / open questions:
- Does the runtime evict partial KV entries on memory pressure causing tail spikes? (saw one OOM-ish kernel handoff in expB)
- Should try combining small batch + q3f for long seq to hit cost + better tail than q3f alone.
- Add an "artifact" column next time: binary/trace link for p95 investigations.

End mini-playbook — export weekly into shared inference notebook.
